clips.text: Eight years day trading. If you have any trading questions, I'm bored, getting high today and not trading. Fidelity banned me because I was making thousands of trades per week, and retail brokers do not tolerate that. You gotta pay for that volume. It says ten percent gain over one year, but I really made about thirty percent APY.
clips.text_zh: 有個佬日交易做咗八年。Fidelity 因為佢一星期trade幾千次ban咗佢。broker根本唔想你高volume。帳面一年10%，佢話實際係30% APY。我prop firm同CFD仲輸緊，又係學費lol。
clips.text_en_b1: Eight years day trading. If you have any trading questions, I'm bored, getting high today and not trading. Fidelity banned me because I was making thousands of trades per week, and retail brokers do not tolerate that. You gotta pay for that volume. clips.text_en_b2: After eight years of day trading, I am bored today, getting high and staying out of the markets, so if you have any trading questions, go ahead and ask. Fidelity banned me because I was putting through thousands of trades per week, and retail brokers simply do not put up with that kind of volume unless you pay for it. The statement shows a ten percent gain over one year, although I actually made roughly thirty percent APY once you factor everything in properly.
clips.text_en_c1: After eight years of day trading, I find myself with little to occupy the afternoon—bored, getting high, and deliberately sitting out the markets—so if anyone has trading questions, now is as good a time as any. Fidelity ultimately banned me for executing thousands of trades per week; retail brokers simply will not tolerate that kind of activity without extracting their pound of flesh. You have to pay for that volume one way or another. My statements show a ten percent gain over one year, yet once you adjust for the real picture, I actually cleared roughly thirty percent APY.
clips.text_en_c2: After eight years of day trading, the poster is sitting out the session, bored and getting high, and has invited any trading questions that happen to come up. Fidelity barred the account outright because the activity ran to thousands of trades each week, a tempo retail brokerages simply refuse to absorb without exacting a price for the volume. The headline figure on the year reads as a ten percent gain, yet the real compounded result sits nearer thirty percent annualized. That gap between the tidy reported number and the lived APY is the sort of detail that only surfaces once someone has ground through enough cycles to know how brokers, fills, and stated returns routinely diverge under heavy retail flow.
clips.source_hint: High-volume day trader banned by a retail broker—mirrors his prop firm and CFD grind and losses-as-tuition mindset.

clips.text: RC buys 7,780,000 shares of BBBY and sixty-to-eighty strike calls worth about 1.67 million shares in March 2022. He sells the shares and calls in August, sits down with Carl Icahn in October, then offers four hundred million for BBBY in December. PitchBook later lists BBBYQ as sold via leveraged buyout.
clips.text_zh: RC 2022年買咗差不多778萬股BBBY，仲有一堆call。之後sell晒，再同Carl Icahn傾，又offer四億買BBBY。而家BBBYQ破產重整，有人當係大棋。我而家月薪捱，呢啲meme債股再入多一口都係學費。
clips.text_en_b1: RC buys 7,780,000 shares of BBBY and sixty-to-eighty strike calls worth about 1.67 million shares in March 2022. He sells the shares and calls in August, sits down with Carl Icahn in October, then offers four hundred million for BBBY in December. PitchBook later lists BBBYQ as sold via leveraged buyout.
clips.text_en_b2: In March 2022, RC picks up 7,780,000 shares of BBBY along with sixty-to-eighty strike calls that cover about 1.67 million shares. He then sells both the shares and the calls in August, sits down with Carl Icahn in October, and by December puts forward a four hundred million offer for BBBY. PitchBook later lists BBBYQ as having been sold through a leveraged buyout, which ties the whole sequence together after those earlier moves.
clips.text_en_c1: In March 2022, RC acquired 7,780,000 shares of BBBY together with sixty-to-eighty strike calls representing roughly 1.67 million underlying shares. By August he had liquidated both the equity position and the options; that October he sat down with Carl Icahn, and in December he put forward a formal offer of four hundred million for the company itself. PitchBook would later catalogue BBBYQ as having been disposed of through a leveraged buyout. The sequence—accumulation, complete exit, high-profile meeting, then a formal bid—has fuelled no end of speculation among those who still track the ticker's messy afterlife on the boards.
clips.text_en_c2: In March 2022, RC acquired 7,780,000 shares of BBBY together with sixty-to-eighty strike calls economically equivalent to roughly 1.67 million shares. By August those shares and calls had been sold; October brought a sit-down with Carl Icahn, and December produced a four-hundred-million offer for the company itself. PitchBook subsequently recorded BBBYQ as having changed hands through a leveraged buyout. The sequence—block accumulation, options overlay, full exit, activist meeting, formal bid, and final LBO classification—compresses into a single creditor-style arc whose public timestamps remain unusually clean for a name that spent so long in distress and narrative fog on the boards.
clips.source_hint: Deep /biz/ recovery lore and big swing risk—same energy as his all-in prop and futures bets while cash is tight.

clips.text: Software engineering is doomed. Autistic software dev with a mid-tier CS master's, fully remote in the middle of nowhere over five years, grinding backend Node and PHP slop. Company quietly preparing layoffs. Once a month some recruiter slides into LinkedIn for an HR screen that goes nowhere.
clips.text_zh: /g/有人講software engineering完咗。自閉backend，remote五年，公司準備layoff，LinkedIn recruiter都係垃圾screen。我做測量助理仲要考HKIE，AI連藍領都要食，白間文職更加危。靠AI續命都未必夠。
clips.text_en_b1: Software engineering is doomed. Autistic software dev with a mid-tier CS master's, fully remote in the middle of nowhere over five years, grinding backend Node and PHP slop. Company quietly preparing layoffs. Once a month some recruiter slides into LinkedIn for an HR screen that goes nowhere.
clips.text_en_b2: Software engineering looks doomed if you ask me. I am an autistic software dev with a mid-tier CS master's who has worked fully remote from the middle of nowhere for over five years, grinding out backend Node and PHP slop the whole time. The company is quietly preparing layoffs, and once a month some recruiter slides into my LinkedIn for an HR screen that goes nowhere, which only underlines how shaky the job market has become for people in my position.
clips.text_en_c1: Software engineering, as a stable career path, increasingly looks doomed. I am the proverbial autistic software developer holding a mid-tier CS master's, working fully remote from the middle of nowhere for over five years while grinding through backend Node and PHP slop that nobody will remember. The company, for its part, has been quietly preparing layoffs, which hardly inspires confidence. Roughly once a month some recruiter slides into my LinkedIn messages proposing an HR screen that, almost without exception, goes absolutely nowhere. The whole pipeline feels stuck between automation anxiety and endless dead-end outreach.
clips.text_en_c2: Software engineering, the poster argues, is simply doomed. The self-description is an autistic developer holding a mid-tier computer-science master’s, fully remote for more than five years from the middle of nowhere, still grinding backend Node and PHP slop while the employer quietly readies layoffs. Once a month a recruiter materializes on LinkedIn, steers the conversation into an HR screen, and then vanishes without a trace of progress. The combination of geographic isolation, commodity stack work, and performative inbound interest that never converts has become the entire texture of the job market as experienced from inside that arrangement, with no signal that the next cycle will look materially different.
clips.source_hint: Remote white-collar AI layoff anxiety hits his fear that surveying work and the license grind still get automated.

clips.text: Now that I am in my thirties with over a decade of lifting, jiu-jitsu and boxing, it is so fun mogging the zoomer twinks at the gym and beating them in class. The twenty-two-year-olds who acted like cunts when I was eighteen get humiliated daily. When they squat three plates for shitty reps, I bench three plates paused.
clips.text_zh: 有個三十歲健身佬，練重訓、柔術、拳擊超過十年，而家專門mog gym入面啲zoomer。以前18歲被22歲串，而家反殺，bench同佢哋squat對住恥辱。肥仔信今日又叫我去gym，三十歲單身更要練，唔好廢。
clips.text_en_b1: Now that I am in my thirties with over a decade of lifting, jiu-jitsu and boxing, it is so fun mogging the zoomer twinks at the gym and beating them in class. clips.text_en_b2: Now that I am in my thirties with over a decade of lifting, jiu-jitsu and boxing behind me, it is genuinely fun mogging the zoomer twinks at the gym and beating them in class. The twenty-two-year-olds who acted like cunts when I was eighteen get humiliated on a daily basis, which never gets old. When they squat three plates for shitty reps, I bench three plates paused, so the gap in training quality shows up immediately whenever we end up side by side.
clips.text_en_c1: Now that I am in my thirties, with over a decade of lifting, jiu-jitsu and boxing behind me, there is a particular satisfaction in mogging the zoomer twinks at the gym and systematically beating them in class. The twenty-two-year-olds who acted like absolute cunts when I was eighteen now find themselves humiliated on a daily basis, which has become something of a routine spectacle. When they squat three plates for a handful of shitty, incomplete reps, I bench three plates paused and fully controlled, without any of the usual gym-floor theatrics that pass for intensity among that cohort.
clips.text_en_c2: Now in his thirties with more than a decade of lifting, jiu-jitsu, and boxing behind him, the poster finds sustained amusement in mogging zoomer twinks at the gym and beating them in class. The same twenty-two-year-olds who behaved like cunts when he was eighteen absorb daily humiliation under the new hierarchy. When they squat three plates for sloppy, incomplete reps, he benches three plates with a deliberate pause. Longevity in the weight room and on the mats has inverted the old social order: the cohort that once set the tone now supplies the contrast, and the physical gap is re-demonstrated often enough that it no longer feels like an accident of a single session.
clips.source_hint: Thirty-year-old gym dominance story maps straight onto his lifting anxiety and sessions with 肥仔信.

clips.text: I am no longer asking, anon. Talk about anime you really wished had more seasons. Not the safe answers only—name the shows that ended too early or got rushed, and why another cour would have fixed them.
clips.text_zh: /a/有人逼大家講：邊套anime你真心恨佢唔夠季數。Gundam 00、Demon Slayer、Attack on Titan我都追過，完得太快或者填太密都難受。考牌同trade輸錢嘅夜晚，淨係翻舊番最穩。
clips.text_en_b1: I am no longer asking, anon. Talk about anime you really wished had more seasons. Not the safe answers only—name the shows that ended too early or got rushed, and why another cour would have fixed them.
clips.text_en_b2: I am no longer asking politely, anon. Talk about anime you really wished had more seasons, and skip the safe answers that everyone always names. Point out the shows that ended too early or got rushed in the final stretch, and explain why another cour would have fixed the pacing or the character arcs. Whenever a series wraps before the source material can breathe, the ending usually falls flat, which is exactly why those extra episodes would have mattered.
clips.text_en_c1: I am no longer asking politely, anon; I am stating the brief outright. Talk about the anime you genuinely wished had been granted more seasons—not the safe, endlessly recycled answers that surface every time this topic appears, but the shows that ended too early or were conspicuously rushed in their final stretch. Name them specifically, and explain why another cour would have fixed the structural problems: unresolved arcs, truncated character work, or finales that felt more like budget contingencies than deliberate conclusions. The board has seen enough vague nostalgia; concrete cases are what actually sustain the thread.
clips.text_en_c2: The poster is no longer asking politely. The demand is for anime titles people genuinely wish had received more seasons—not the safe consensus answers, but the shows that terminated too early or were visibly rushed, together with a concrete account of why another cour would have repaired them. Incomplete arcs, truncated character work, and adaptations that slammed into the source’s midsection without room to land are the wounds under discussion. The thread wants specificity: name the series, name the failure mode, and name the structural fix an extra cour could have bought, rather than recycling the usual critically insulated favorites that already escaped with their reputations intact.
clips.source_hint: Open season-wishlist thread lets him vent about Gundam 00, Demon Slayer and AOT after exam and trading stress.
